clue.text: Races divided by southern state's method of riot control

indicators.note: divided by says the first word is split open with the second set in the gap

parts.note: races as a verb means tears along at speed
GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a state in the southern US

explanation.surface: A report on how one southern US state handles rioting crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Races' looks like contests but is a verb, dashing about; the 's after state is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is an irritant sprayed by police to disperse crowds, a standard tool for quelling disorder.

clue.text: Produce designs on skin and make lace as well

parts.note: to tat is to make lace by knotting thread with a shuttle
as well means too, also

explanation.surface: Someone who both inks skin and makes lace as a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink permanent pictures into skin with needles is what a tattooist does.

clue.text: Deeds required for legal proceed, ings

definitions.meaning: lawsuits brought in court, as in bringing several against the firm; the stray comma is a print artefact

explanation.surface: A remark that documents are needed when going to court.
explanation.walkthrough: The text as held splits 'proceedings' with a stray comma; the clue is a plain double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts done are actions, and a lawsuit is also called an action at law.

clue.text: Gunners in shop get faulty ammunition

indicators.note: faulty suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Artillerymen buy defective shells from a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges RA plus SHOP plus GET; 'in' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon, a historic kind of artillery round.

clue.text: Do daily work annually?

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning lady; doing her work once a year means the big seasonal tidy-up

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a job done every day being done once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like 'every day', but in British usage a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorough once-a-year house clean, traditionally in the warmer months, is what the phrase names.

clue.text: By no means a common type of butterfly

definitions.text: By no means a common type of butterfly

parts.words: By no means a common type of butterfly
parts.note: read as royalty, a king is by no means a commoner; read as an insect, it names a well-known orange-and-black species

explanation.surface: A remark that some butterfly is rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' looks like 'widespread', but it hints at a commoner, the opposite of a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning king or queen is no commoner, and the migratory orange butterfly shares the royal title.

clue.text: Silent relative

definitions.meaning: saying nothing, as in 'keep it quiet'
a family member, here a mother

explanation.definitionFit: Keeping quiet is the idiom 'staying schtum', and a mother is a close family member.

clue.text: Synthetic material US city produced with 50% of capital

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: fifty per cent of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: the capital here is London, Britain's capital city

explanation.surface: A fabric made jointly in New York and part of a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' keeps the first half of LONDON, LON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a man-made polymer fibre used for stockings and rope.

clue.text: Sovereign, possibly, as profit from bookmaking enterprise

definitions.meaning: a sovereign is one example of the ruling family's members
bookmaking here is making books: an author's payment per copy sold

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a monarch would profit from running a betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaking' suggests betting, but it means writing and publishing books.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a member of the crowned class, and an author's per-copy payment carries the same name.

clue.text: Social worker meeting for work with sweetheart

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment for a sweetheart
a bee is a gathering for a joint task, as in a sewing bee

explanation.surface: A council social worker meets a client and their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' sounds like a care professional, but it is an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Hive insects live in colonies, and the sterile females are called workers.

clue.text: Four-letter word producing great agitation in public vehicle

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the vehicle's name

parts.note: a tram is a public transport vehicle on rails

indicators.note: agitation means a stirring-up, so the word great is churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swears on a bus and causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitation' rearranges the word great into ETRAG, which 'in' places inside the vehicle word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, from Greek tetra (four) plus gramma (letter).

clue.text: Provide, as Macduff was enjoined to do?

definitions.meaning: to supply, as in arranging transport for guests

definitions.text: as Macduff was enjoined to do?
definitions.meaning: Macbeth's last speech says '..., Macduff', urging him to attack

explanation.surface: Asking what supplying something has to do with a Shakespeare line.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half quotes Macbeth's challenge to Macduff in their final fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something on is to supply or arrange it, such as food or entertainment.

clue.text: Bracing air somebody associated with wizard place

parts.note: Oz is the land of The Wizard of Oz
one means a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Someone linked to a magic land breathes fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh seaside air was popularly called this, from a belief that its supposed gas was invigorating.

clue.text: Rose's scent cannot be changed in such an insignificant way

definitions.text: Rose's scent cannot be changed in such an insignificant way

parts.words: Rose's scent cannot be changed in such an insignificant way
parts.note: Juliet says a rose by any other name would smell as sweet: changing what it is called alters it only in name

explanation.surface: A gardener's remark that a flower's perfume never changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to Romeo and Juliet: renaming a rose changes it only in a trivial, in-name-only sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something altered only in name, in a token way, is changed in title alone.

clue.text: Such movies I reviewed as harmful

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking over again and reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film critic calls certain films damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges SUCH MOVIES I; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischievous can mean causing damage or trouble, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: According to circumstances, subjective or objective?

definitions.meaning: depending on how things turn out
in grammar the subjective and objective are cases of a noun or pronoun, so the form depends on which case applies

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about whether a judgement is personal or impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subjective or objective' looks philosophical, but they are grammatical cases.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means depending on the situation, and literally names which grammatical case applies.

clue.text: Play without dialogue

parts.note: a drama with no exchange between characters is one with a single performer speaking alone

explanation.surface: A description of a silent stage piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without dialogue' suggests mime, but it means one speaker, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage piece for a single performer has no exchange of lines between actors.

clue.text: Cricketer overcome by loyal person's critical remark

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcome by puts the cricketer below the loyal person

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, staunch friend
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman is beaten by a fan's harsh words.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'overcome by' puts BAT beneath BRICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is an unkind or hostile comment, from the brick fragment once thrown as a missile.

clue.text: To introduce variation and righten?

definitions.meaning: to vary something by trying different versions
righten is a reshuffle of the letters of the two words ring the

explanation.surface: A puzzling comment about making changes and putting things right.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: RIGHTEN is a rearrangement of RING THE, so it shows the phrase's first two words being varied.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell-ringers work through every order of the bells; the idiom means to vary something repeatedly.

clue.text: Dined in home that's extremely dainty

indicators.note: in tells us the meal word sits inside the home word

parts.note: a nest is a home, for birds or people
dined means ate

explanation.surface: Eating at home is the most refined thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of neat means most trim and tidy, as dainty implies delicately fine.

clue.text: Bridge player arranged to be in for rubber

parts.note: E is East, one of the four players at bridge

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge player is set to take part in a rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TO BE IN to BONITE; 'rubber' looks like a bridge term but is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebonite is hard vulcanised rubber, a dark material once used for combs and pipe stems.

clue.text: Take charge and take weight off someone's shoulders?

definitions.meaning: humorously, removing the topmost load is decapitating someone

explanation.surface: Taking over and relieving someone of a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a grim joke: taking the top weight off the shoulders removes the cranium.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means be the leader; as one, it means to cut off at the neck.

clue.text: Dispute old-fashioned measure held back by reform

indicators.note: held means the reform word holds the measure inside it

parts.note: reform means change

indicators.note: back means the measure word is read in reverse

parts.note: an ell was an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Arguing that an outdated unit was blocked by a reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the measure into LLE and 'held' puts it inside the reform word; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge a claim is to question or contest it.

clue.text: Deposit for a house

definitions.meaning: to place something with a bank or authority, as in filing a complaint
a small dwelling, such as a gatehouse or hunting cabin

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit to buy a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To file a complaint is to put it in formally, and a gatekeeper's cottage is a small dwelling.

clue.text: People in group compelled to work hard

definitions.meaning: a crowd moving together, as in people arriving in their hundreds
past tense of the verb meaning push someone hard

explanation.surface: A gang of people was forced into hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds of people are described as arriving in herds, and pushing staff hard is past-tense urging.

clue.text: Crook pinching pound to get whisky, for example

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the crook word grips the pound inside

parts.note: a crook is a bend or curve
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A thief steals money to buy Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a thief and 'pinching' like stealing, but they are a curve and a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Many whiskies are mixtures of malts and grains, so one is an example of such a mixture.

clue.text: In game of cards, holding 'top card, a preference for double

annotationWithheld.clue: In game of cards, holding 'top card, a preference for double

clue.text: Bar this grassland for cereal crop

indicators.note: for here means that the word given first, plus this answer, stands for the crop, so take it away

parts.note: barley is a cereal crop
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fence off this pasture to grow grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Bar this' as BAR followed by the answer: together they make the cereal crop, so the crop less BAR is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ley is land sown with grass temporarily, a pasture field in arable rotation.

clue.text: Unsteady scavenger at end of bay

parts.note: a totter is a British term for a rag-and-bone collector who scavenges rubbish

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word bay

explanation.surface: A scavenger staggers at the far end of a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: TOTTER is old British slang for someone who scavenges in rubbish tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means shaky and wobbly on one's feet, likely to fall.

clue.text: Growth, in the main, filling offspring with wonder

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the wonder word goes into the offspring word

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants
awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: Children's growth fills them with amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, so 'Growth, in the main' means a plant that grows in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp and wrack are marine algae, plants that grow in the sea.
